title: SYSK Selects: How the Rosetta Stone Works
summary: SYSK Selects rerun, chosen by Josh, of the 2013 episode "How the Rosetta Stone Works." The hosts explain that the Rosetta Stone is not a key to hieroglyphics but a Ptolemaic-era government decree inscribed in Greek, hieroglyphic, and demotic script. They cover why hieroglyphics were lost (suppression after Egypt fell under Greek, Roman, and later rulers, and the rise of Coptic and Arabic), the stone's discovery by French soldiers during Napoleon's Egypt campaign, the Institute of Egypt, the British-French rivalry between Thomas Young and Jean-Francois Champollion, Hoopolo's false translation, Champollion's cartouche breakthrough deciphering the name Ramesses, the stone's transfer to Britain, and Egypt's repatriation requests. The episode ends with listener mail.

segments.title: Selects intro by Josh
segments.summary: Josh introduces his chosen 2013 episode on the Rosetta Stone, explaining its role in deciphering hieroglyphics.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts joke about being cold in the studio, their lack of visits to Egypt, Egyptology as a field, and Napoleon's real height versus the French inch myth.

segments.title: What the Rosetta Stone is
segments.summary: The stone is described as a black basalt stela, about the size of a heavy coffee table, and is a government decree inscribed in Greek, hieroglyphics, and demotic. The decree praises Ptolemy V and was issued by priests at Memphis. The stone is important for the three-language inscription rather than its content.

segments.title: Egyptian writing systems
segments.summary: Hieroglyphics were a sacred script, demotic was a shorthand, vulgar form, and hieratic sat between them and was used for business. The three-language decree was meant to be readable by literate Egyptians.

segments.title: Loss of hieroglyphics
segments.summary: After Cleopatra, Egypt was ruled by Greeks, Romans, and others. Christianity and new rulers suppressed the old gods and their sacred script. Demotic evolved into Coptic, which was later replaced by Arabic, and hieroglyphics were lost. Egyptian buildings were dismantled for building material.

segments.title: Napoleon's Egypt campaign and the stone's discovery
segments.summary: Napoleon invaded Egypt partly to cut off British access to the Nile and threaten India. The British navy destroyed the French fleet, stranding the French for years. Napoleon created the Institute of Egypt of scholars who studied Egypt. A French lieutenant, Pierre Francois Bouchard, found the stone built into a wall and it was studied by the Institute.

segments.title: Britain takes the stone and the decipherment race
segments.summary: The French made copies before the stone went to the British under the Treaty of Alexandria. Thomas Young and Jean-Francois Champollion raced to decipher it. Silvestre de Sacy worked on the Greek and demotic, and Akerblad worked on demotic. Hoopolo's centuries-old false translation, which treated hieroglyphs as purely symbolic, had misled scholars.

segments.title: Champollion's breakthrough and Egyptology's birth
segments.summary: Young identified cartouches as royal names and Ptolemy in one. Champollion used the cartouche of Ramesses to show hieroglyphs were phonetic, establishing Egyptology. The hosts describe the rivalry between Britain and France over credit and the 1972 display dispute. Champollion later argued for keeping antiquities in Egypt.

segments.title: Repatriation dispute over the stone
segments.summary: The stone remains in the British Museum since 1802, apart from a brief stay in France. Egypt requested its return in 2003 and Britain offered a replica. Major museums rejected repatriation. Egypt was refused again around 2012 for the Grand Egyptian Museum opening.

segments.title: Outro
segments.summary: Hosts close the episode with a pointer to the website article. Remaining segment is listener mail and sign-off.
